# the contributor audit: exact interpolation at three actual stationary roots

Source: `candidate 03420419c4771251`.
Full independent read: **PASS**, for b=(a,c,B,B) with a,c>1/3. The source now correctly takes its least-active candidate among global maxima; its local corollary explicitly assumes independent active rows.

The same-side and triangular-section arguments force the common unoriented split. Equal central coordinates force equal heights by the stated diagonal ordering identity. Normalizing those heights to -1 is legitimate for the ordinary simplex problem. The through-b constraint then gives the exact affine line a p+c q=2B.

The stationarity cubic is derived from the actual captured-coordinate equation, so it does not introduce the spurious equal-positive-height branch that would arise from checking only the excluded centroid coordinates. Every actual section is a root. Rank three and the sum-zero margin identity require three distinct unoriented sections, and the nonzero cubic leading coefficient means that these are its three distinct roots. Only actual positive p,q roots are used.

The reciprocal-stiffness identity is a rational remainder identity modulo that explicit cubic. All coefficients of the quadratic interpolant are displayed. Its denominator E is strictly positive from 0<B<1/6 and |a-c|<1/3, and its quadratic coefficient is strictly positive. The formula makes no assertion about convexity away from the actual roots. At the middle root the strict secant gap is exactly the positive quadratic coefficient times the product of its two root gaps.

The three actual signed normal coefficients sum to zero and have zero p-weighted sum. This fixes the middle coefficient's opposite sign and the exact outer interpolation weights. If the outer caps capture the central pair, two positive directions violate the joint index. In the remaining orientation, the good middle row's antisymmetric gain and the two bad outer losses have the stated inverse scaling by their actual normal multipliers. Pair symmetry makes the threshold correction zero in this channel; no general uncorrected direction is used.

Optimal distribution of the funding is the ordinary parallel quadratic cost, and the strict three-root reciprocal gap proves that the middle gain exceeds it. The displayed row path preserves every column and stays feasible in both signs. The common gradient cancels its first derivative, giving an actual local improvement.

The proof excludes this entire one-equal-central-pair/two-noncentral-coordinate class, including unequal noncentral coordinates. It does not imply that a general stationary configuration has an equal pair. No symmetry reduction or unrestricted reciprocal convexity has entered.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
